explanation: Brazil gave raw materials and ground for air bases, and received the capital for a steel industry. Wikipedia states the order of events. In 1942, after the American proposal to finance the CSN, United States forces established air bases along Brazil’s north-eastern coast. It also states the bargain, settled in July 1940. In exchange for raw materials the United States provided equipment, technical assistance and financing for a Brazilian steel mill. Roosevelt’s Good Neighbor policy is where the financing sat, and reports at the time said the United States had a plan to invade the Northeast if Vargas insisted on neutrality. What Brazil bought with the Atlantic narrows was the plant at Volta Redonda.
